newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescued French sailor does "lot of smiling".
newsitem.headline: Rescued French sailor does "lot of smiling".

text.p: A French solo sailor plucked by helicopter from icy seas near Antarctica on Thursday was in "extremely good" health after his ordeal and could not stop smiling, the captain of an Australian navy frigate said.
Thierry Dubois, 29, was rescued after four days in a small life raft and brought aboard HMAS Adelaide, suffering only mild hypothermia and some sores from exposure to water on his feet and hands.
Dubois capsized on Sunday in the Southern Ocean between Australia and the Antarctic and was thrown a life raft by a rescue plane the following day.
He was winched from the raft on Thursday a few hours before the rescue of fellow racer Tony Bullimore of Britain.
"When we brought him on board this morning he was smiling broadly," said the Adelaide's Captain Raydon Gates.
"His conditions is extremely good considering the ordeal he has been through."
Gates said Dubois's first word was 'Thanks', adding: "He did very little talking but a lot of smiling."
Dubois was to be treated for hypothermia by navy doctors. As soon as his condition was stabilised, he would be contacting his family in France, who were anxiously awaiting his news, Gates added.
